messages:
Maya: Quick proposal — add a paid "predictive prewarm" add-on for Dedicated customers. It'd proactively warm KV cache + model context for top-N tenants based on short-term forecast so microbursts hit warm state. Thinking: opt-in tiers, forecast horizon, and launch criteria. :thinking:
Sam: Sounds useful for latency-sensitive customers. What's the basic UX/contract? Do we promise X ms p95 for bursts? Any limits on burst size?
Maya: UX: customer enables a toggle + selects commitment tier (none / standard / premium). Platform keeps warm replicas + runs a 5–15m short-horizon forecast. SLA proposal: premium -> p95 burst latency <= baseline SLO * 1.1 for the first 2k tokens of a burst. Standard -> best-effort.
TJ: Implementation notes: this requires KV cache prefill + model weight resident guarantees on pool nodes. We need a prewarm controller that can schedule prefill jobs without disrupting normal batching. Also need a way to pin a tiny fraction of GPU memory for warm KV pages.
Raj: Alerting/telemetry we need: prewarm hit rate, added memory pressure, prewarm eviction count, and warm-burst latency delta. Also circuit-breaker if prewarm causes OOMs.
Elaine: From sales convo yesterday: two large customers asked for something like this but want deterministic guarantees and billing as "burst credits". They expect clear metering. We should map tiers to monthly committed burst credits and overage unit price.
Sam: Agreed on metering. We also need pricing mockups to simulate per-tenant cost. Can we get a rough cost model: extra N GPU-minutes per prewarm per tenant * #tenants?
TJ: Rough sketch: prewarm cost ~= (#prefills/day) * (prefill_duration_minutes) * GPU_hourly_cost / 60. Prefill_duration depends on KV size and model; estimate 1–6 minutes typical. We should prototype on a 1-model, 3-tenant sim.
Maya: Launch checklist idea: 1) telemetry product (Raj) 2) admission controls + circuit-breaker (TJ/Raj) 3) billing + tiers (Elaine/Product) 4) RFC doc + customer runbook (Maya) 5) small pilot (1 customer)
Raj: For telemetry, suggest these KPIs: prewarm_success_rate, avg_prefill_time, p50/p95 warm-latency-delta, oom_incidents, and prewarm-cost-per-10k-burst-tokens. Need to hook into Console dashboards.
Elaine: Marketing/comms angle: call it "BurstGuard" or "Predictive Warm"? Customers like short names. Also need exact language for guarantees vs best-effort.
TJ: Quick config snippet for controller we could expose to ops/devs:```yaml
prewarm:
  enabled: true
  tier: premium
  forecast_window_m: 10
  max_prefill_concurrency: 3
  kv_prefill_bytes_limit: 500MB
```
Maya: Nice. Can the controller respect node-level headroom so we don't impact non-opted tenants?
TJ: Yes — controller must check pool_free_memory_pct and backlog before scheduling. Fail-safe: if pool_free_memory_pct < 12% => skip prewarm.
Sam: Risks: (1) hidden cost to infra (2) complexity in autoscaler interplay (3) observable regressions. We should lock to Dedicated pools only for launch.
Maya: Pilot criteria: signed pilot NDA, commit to collect telemetry, agree on up to 2-week trial. If pilot achieves >70% prewarm hit and no OOMs, proceed to beta.
Elaine: Sales asks to build a one-pager with pricing bands: 10k burst tokens/month, 50k, 200k with discounts. I'll draft.
Raj: Ops note: add alert routes to oncall-sre for prewarm-oom and prewarm-failure-spike (pager after 3 consecutive fails)
OpsBot: Reminder: product-capacity-sync scheduled Thu 11:00. Please add prewarm pilot agenda item.
Maya: Next steps: TJ + Raj prototype perf/telemetry by EOD next Tue, Elaine to draft pricing, I'll write detailed RFC for review. :thumbsup:
